title: Google’s free streaming service now lets you pick shows and movies to watch
summary: Google TV Freeplay has expanded from a live-channel streaming platform to include video-on-demand with over 10,000 titles. The service also added 300+ live channels spanning news, sports, and entertainment programming.
content:
Google TV Freeplay, the company's free, ad-supported streaming service, now supports video on demand. Instead of tuning into Google TV Freeplay's selection of always-on channels, you can now choose from over 10,000 shows and movies to watch whenever you want.
The update introduces titles like Lady Bird, Seventeen Again, and Hell's Kitchen, according to Google's announcement. The company has also expanded its live TV lineup to include more than 300 channels dedicated to news, sports, reality TV, true crime, and more. title: Another OpenAI executive takes off
summary: Brad Lightcap, OpenAI's special projects lead and former COO, is departing after eight years to pursue new ventures. He will remain engaged with the company's mission during a transition period.
content:
Brad Lightcap, OpenAI's special projects lead and the company's former COO, announced his departure after an eight-year stint at the AI lab. In an internal memo he later posted to X, Lightcap told colleagues he'd be starting "something new."
"Over the last few months, I've been focused on the next horizon and what would stand in the way of mission success," Lightcap wrote. "I believe there are a few important new things the world will need to get right as we enter this next period. I … am excited to help you all advance the mission from a different vantage point." He added that he'd still be around for the next few weeks.

title: The budget-friendly Pixel Buds 2a are even cheaper right now
summary: Google's Pixel Buds 2a are currently on sale for $99, down from their standard $129 price at major retailers. The wireless earbuds feature active noise cancellation and Gemini AI integration at a competitive price point.
content:
The Google Pixel Buds 2a in hazel. | Image: The Verge	

Looking for great pair of earbuds that work particularly well with Android phones? The Google Pixel Buds 2a are currently discounted to $99 (usually $129) at various retailers, including Amazon, Best Buy, and directly from Google. These very capable Bluetooth earbuds come in four colors, with a lightweight fit that helps them disappear into your ears. With ANC and transparency mode support, and a close integration with Gemini, they’re a great choice for anyone with a Pixel or other Android device.
Pixel Buds 2a
Google’s latest pair of wireless earbuds feature crisp sound quality, a comfortable design, and solid active noise cancellation, which is great considering the budget-friendly price tag. They even offer built-in support for Gemini and, unlike the entry-level AirPods, a purple option! Read our review.

Where to Buy:

 $129 $99 at Amazon
 $129 $99 at Google
 $129 $99 at Best Buy

My colleague David Pierce reviewed the Pixel Buds 2a on their release in October of 2025, and was impressed by the excellent sound quality, impressive ANC and transparency modes, and comfortable fit, particularly at the price point. The biggest complaint we had about these earbuds is that they lack some of the advanced features when paired with an iPhone or iPad, similar to how AirPods don’t support their full feature suite with Android phones.
Read our Pixel Buds 2a review.

title: Google’s upcoming Pixel phones are for the fans, even if its launch event isn’t
summary: Google's Pixel 11 launch will feature comedian Trevor Noah hosting a celebrity-driven show, continuing the company's shift toward entertainment over technical specifications. Last year's similar approach generated 8.4 million YouTube viewers.
content:
The Pixel 11 Pro has a flashy new light on the back. | Image: Google	

Last year's Made by Google event for the Pixel 10 resembled a late night talk show, complete with Jimmy Fallon as host, and it aired an hour after the phones were revealed. Spec dives and executive appearances were replaced with celebrity cameos and awkward skits, to the confusion of many diehard Pixel fans. But it served its purpose in reaching a broader audience: Last year's stream racked up 8.4 million viewers on YouTube; the launch the year before only managed 1.4 million.

title: Made by Google 2026: all the Pixel news and announcements
summary: Google will unveil new Pixel 11 models on August 12th, including a Pixel Fold and Pixel Watch 5, with a possible Pixel Tag tracker. Preorder windows and the livestream hosted by Trevor Noah will occur on August 12th.
content:
Google is gearing up to reveal a bunch of new Pixel devices on August 12th. A series of leaks leading up to the event suggest that the Pixel 11 lineup will come in an array of colors, with signs pointing to a built-in light coming to Pro models. Teasers from Google also indicate that it will show off a next-gen Pixel Fold alongside a Pixel Watch 5 in four different finishes. There might be a new Pixel Tag tracker as well.
Google may take the wraps off the new devices well ahead of its Made by Google livestream. On Google’s website, the countdown for preorders ends on August 12th at 10AM ET — eight hours before its event at 6PM ET. Comedian Trevor Noah will host this year’s show, featuring notable guests like NBA star Stephen Curry, podcaster Alex Cooper, Indian cricketer Shubman Gill, and Japanese actress Ayami Nakajo. We’ll be live blogging the event, so stay tuned!
Follow along for all the latest news about Google’s Pixel devices.

title: An unreleased Anthropic model made progress on one of math’s biggest unsolved problems
summary: Anthropic's unreleased AI model made surprising progress on the Riemann hypothesis, a major unsolved mathematical problem for over 150 years. While not solved, the advancement demonstrates AI's potential for cutting-edge mathematical research.
content: For more than 150 years, the Riemann hypothesis has stood as one of the major unsolved problems in mathematics. Anthropic hasn't solved it — but the company's models made more progress than you might expect.

title: Apple could help you prove your iPhone photos aren’t deepfakes
summary: Apple is developing an iOS 27 feature that embeds provenance metadata into iPhone photos at capture to prove authenticity and detect AI-generated images. The Apple Reference Image system will be disabled by default upon rollout.
content:
Apple is seemingly developing an iOS feature that can verify when a photograph was taken using an iPhone camera. 9to5Mac reports that the iOS 27 beta 5 includes code references for an "Apple Reference Image" system that can embed provenance metadata into iPhone photographs at the point of capture - enabling users to prove where the photo originated, and that it isn't AI fakery.
